mechanism: Core's CWallet::blockDisconnected ends with SetLastBlockProcessed(block.height - 1, *block.prev_hash) (refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/wallet.cpp:1598), and SetLastBlockProcessed is SetLastBlockProcessedInMem followed by WriteBestBlock() (:681-687, :4534-4547), so EVERY disconnect syncs the rolled-back locator to the wallet file. blockConnected by contrast calls only SetLastBlockProcessedInMem (:1536) and persists at the end just when a wallet tx changed or height % 144 == 0 (:1550-1552). Ours mirrors the connect side exactly -- wallet-block-connected (src/wallet/wallet-tx.lisp:1101-1132) sets the in-memory pair and calls wallet-write-best-block only under the same two conditions -- but wallet-block-disconnected (:1135-1165) ends by SETF-ing wallet-last-block-hash to the disconnected header's prev-block and wallet-last-block-height to (1- height), and returns. Nothing on the disconnect path reaches wallet-write-best-block (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:941-961); its only callers are create-wallet (:1033), the connect-side cadence, scan-for-wallet-transactions' save-progress, wallet-attach-chain, backupwallet and unload-wallet.
consequence: Between a reorg and the next qualifying connection the on-disk bestblock_nomerkle record names a block on the abandoned branch while memory holds the correct rolled-back one, so a crash in that window loads a wallet whose locator is stale in the wrong direction. It is bounded rather than wrong: the persisted value is the exponential locator %wallet-chain-locator built from the block index, whose remaining hashes are ancestors still on the active chain, so find-fork-in-active-chain (src/storage/chain.lisp:1455-1473) finds a fork one or a few blocks lower and wallet-attach-chain rescans from there -- correct, just longer. No transaction state is lost, since every wallet tx carries its own confirmation record. The unload path is NOT exposed the way the finding suggests: unload-wallet (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:1299) writes a single-hash locator built from wallet-last-block-hash, which the disconnect has already rolled back to the correct value, so a clean shutdown after a reorg persists the right block.
evidence: Container /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-misc-s3d, warm image, probe-a.lisp under with-wallet-chain-node. A wallet was driven through wallet-block-connected at height 287 (locator forced to disk), wallet-block-connected at 288 (the 144-cadence branch fires, so the h2 locator lands on disk), then wallet-block-disconnected of 288. Output: (:AFTER-CONNECT-H287 :MEM-HEIGHT 287 :MEM-HASH "1cc3adea40eb" :DISK ("1cc3adea40eb")) (:AFTER-CONNECT-H288-CADENCE-PERSISTS :MEM-HEIGHT 288 :MEM-HASH "c942a06c127c" :DISK ("c942a06c127c")) (:AFTER-DISCONNECT-H288 :MEM-HEIGHT 287 :MEM-HASH "1cc3adea40eb" :DISK ("c942a06c127c")). The last line is the divergence: memory correctly names h1@287 while the wallet file still names h2, the block just disconnected. Trap worth recording: the first run showed no write at all at the cadence height because wallet-block-connected's birthday gate (wallet-tx.lisp:1113-1119) returns early for any block whose time predates the wallet birth time by more than 2*TIMESTAMP_WINDOW -- a fixed 2023 timestamp silences the whole hook, and the probe looked like a missing write rather than a skipped block. Ours: src/wallet/wallet-tx.lisp:1135-1165, src/wallet/wallet.lisp:941-961. Core: refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/wallet.cpp:1598, :681-687, :4534-4547, :1550-1552.
fix_shape: Give the disconnect path Core's SetLastBlockProcessed rather than its InMem half: after the in-memory SETF at the end of wallet-block-disconnected, build the locator for the new best block and call wallet-write-best-block, the same call the connect path makes. The disconnect hook has no chain-state argument today, so either thread the chain-state through wallets-block-disconnected / wallet-block-disconnected the way the connect fan-out already does -- which lets %wallet-chain-locator produce a real exponential locator -- or, if that plumbing is unwanted, pass no locator and accept wallet-write-best-block's single-hash fallback, which is still strictly better than leaving the abandoned block on disk. Note the cost Core accepts here: a deep reorg writes one fsynced record per disconnected block, so if that is judged too expensive the honest alternative is to persist once at the END of the reorg rather than not at all. A regression test drives connect(h)/connect(h+1 at a cadence height)/disconnect(h+1) and asserts the on-disk bestblock_nomerkle record names h, not h+1.
